title: Higher direct images commute with filtered colimits
statement:
Let $p\colon X\to Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $A$ a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$.
For every $q$, $R^qp_*$ on sheaves of $A$-modules commutes with filtered colimits and direct sums.

Here $X$ and $Y$ are schemes [def-pc-scheme], and quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. The sites are the small pro-étale sites [sk-def-pe-site], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Module sheaves are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The direct image [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] takes an $A$-module sheaf $M$ to the $p_*A$-module sheaf with sections $(p_*M)(V)=M(X\times_Y V)$. For $q\in\mathbf Z$, $R^qp_*(M)$ means $H^q(Rp_*(M[0]))$, where $M[0]$ is concentrated in degree zero, with right derivation and cohomology as in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Colimits and direct sums are taken in these module-sheaf categories [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

proof.text: For a small filtered diagram (M_i) of A-module sheaves put K_i=M_i[0]. Every K_i vanishes below the common degree a=0. Colimits of module sheaves exist and agree with colimits of the underlying abelian sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]; their termwise colimit is (colim_i M_i)[0], since every other degree is the zero diagram. Apply [det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image] with f=p and its arbitrary ring sheaf mathcal R=A. Its hypotheses are exactly the given quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness and the common bound 0. By the degree-zero-complex meaning of R^q in the statement, it gives colim_i R^q p_*M_i ≅ R^q p_*(colim_i M_i). The comparison is the canonical one: its i-th leg is R^q p_* applied to M_i→colim_j M_j. This proves filtered continuity. The map is p_*A-linear; an isomorphism of underlying abelian sheaves has a p_*A-linear inverse, since applying the map to both sides of a·f^(-1)(n)=f^(-1)(a·n) gives the same section.

source.place: Proof step 1 and Complement; degree-zero specialization of det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image

proof.text: Fix a small family (M_j) indexed by J, and choose once, for each j∈J, bounded-below, termwise injective, K-injective resolutions M_j[0]→I_j using [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution] on the small ringed site (X_proét,A). For each finite subset F⊆J their finite direct sum I_F is K-injective: for an acyclic complex C a chain map C→I_F has finitely many component maps C→I_j, each null-homotopic; the finite tuple of their homotopies is a null-homotopy of the original map. The map (⊕_{j∈F} M_j)[0]→I_F is a quasi-isomorphism: kernels and images of the block-diagonal differential are respectively the finite direct sums of the component kernels and images, so H^r(I_F)=⊕_{j∈F}H^r(I_j). This is also valid for F empty, when I_F=0. By [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image], p_* is sectionwise restriction; it preserves finite biproducts because those are finite products of abelian sheaves, computed sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](2). Consequently p_*I_F=⊕_{j∈F}p_*I_j. Compute Rp_* on these K-injective resolutions by [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] and compute cohomology by the kernel/image formula of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This gives the isomorphism ⊕_{j∈F}R^q p_*M_j→R^q p_*(⊕_{j∈F}M_j). It is the canonical map, since the inclusion of I_j into I_F lifts the inclusion of M_j, and naturality of the derived-functor unit identifies its derived image with that inclusion on cohomology. For F⊆G the inclusions of resolutions induce the inclusions of finite subsums on both sides, so these isomorphisms commute with the transition maps.

proof.text: Let (M_j) now be indexed by any small set J, and let P be the poset of finite subsets F⊆J, including ∅. It is small, nonempty, and filtered: F∪G is a common upper bound, and there are no distinct parallel arrows in a poset. Put M_F=⊕_{j∈F}M_j with the canonical inclusion maps for F⊆G. Then colim_{F∈P}M_F=⊕_{j∈J}M_j. Indeed, a cocone M_F→N is precisely a family M_j→N: restriction to singleton subsets extracts the family, and the finite coproduct universal property reconstructs each cocone leg, including the unique leg on M_∅=0. The two operations are inverse and respect all inclusions. This proves the asserted colimit by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The same argument applies to the family R^q p_*M_j. Both categories have the required colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful].

source.place: Statement: direct sums are filtered colimits of finite subsums; explicit universal-property argument

proof.text: Apply Step 1 to the filtered diagram F↦M_F of Step 3. Step 2 supplies isomorphisms ⊕_{j∈F}R^q p_*M_j ≅ R^q p_*M_F compatible with every F⊆G. Therefore, using Step 3 in the source and target module categories, ⊕_{j∈J}R^q p_*M_j ≅ colim_F R^q p_*M_F ≅ R^q p_*(colim_F M_F) ≅ R^q p_*(⊕_{j∈J}M_j). The composite on the j-th coproduct summand is R^q p_* of the original j-th inclusion, by Step 1 and the finite-sum compatibility in Step 2. The coproduct universal property therefore identifies this composite with the canonical direct-sum comparison. This proves the direct-sum clause, including the empty family.
